top_choice_rationale: P002 (Adonis) remains my first choice on the common criteria. The claim is that his poetry, with the essays as supporting evidence, changed the language and form of an entire poetic tradition through myth, fragmentation and a sustained argument with inherited Arabic forms. Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses are the representative works. The case rests on poetic language, form and sustained span, not on reception, political standing or age. The weakness is evidentiary. The claim concerns Arabic prosody, diction and allusion, which I can judge only through translation and secondary accounts. I cannot confirm that the later collections match the canonical early ones, and no original-language reading is in the supplied evidence. I hold this preference as a judgment under uncertainty. P001 (Cărtărescu) is a close second. His large imaginative architecture is a serious and distinctive achievement, but I cannot verify whether the very long late novels extend or repeat the project, and the translated coverage of his poetry and essays is thin. It would move first if original-language readings failed to support the formal claim for Adonis, or if the later Adonis work proved thin. The 4-to-2 split in round-2 support is not evidence of merit. P000 ranks last because both proposals rest on serious bodies of work, and unresolved translation uncertainty is a reason to read more closely, not to withhold the award. No independent verification of sources is claimed.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. The profile documents no personal or institutional tie to Adonis, Cărtărescu or any other shortlisted writer. My scholarly work on modern poetry, exile literature and the literary fragment is context only, not evidence of preference. As chair I disclose that P002 is my own preferred proposal; conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated in this simulation.
